description: Standardized rules for RESTful API design, versioning, pagination, HTTP status semantics, and error envelopes.

rules.name: Mandatory Collection Pagination
rules.description: All collection endpoints returning arrays of resources (e.g. GET /api/v1/users) must enforce pagination with page/limit or cursor parameters and a maximum page size cap.
rules.rationale: Unbounded queries lead to out-of-memory errors, database starvation, high latency, and Denial of Service (DoS) vulnerabilities.
rules.remediation: Apply pagination middleware or query builder limiters (e.g., max 100 items per request).

rules.name: Explicit API Versioning
rules.description: Public and internal REST endpoints must include an explicit version identifier in the URI path (e.g., `/api/v1/orders`) or via a version header.
rules.rationale: Enables non-breaking contract evolution, backward compatibility, and structured deprecation lifecycles for mobile and web clients.
rules.remediation: Prefix route groups with `/v1/`, `/v2/` or configure header-based API versioning.

rules.name: Standardized Error Envelope (RFC 7807 Problem Details)
rules.description: Error responses (HTTP 4xx and 5xx) must follow the RFC 7807 Problem Details format containing `type`, `title`, `status`, `detail`, and `instance`.
rules.rationale: Uniform error structures simplify client-side error handling, logging, and automated API consumption.
rules.remediation: Centralize global exception handling to serialize errors into RFC 7807 compliant payloads.

rules.name: Strict HTTP Status Code Semantics
rules.description: Prohibits returning HTTP 200 OK for operational errors or exceptions (e.g., returning `{ status: 'error', code: 500 }` with HTTP 200).
rules.rationale: Misleading HTTP statuses break reverse proxy caching, API gateways, health checks, and automated monitoring systems.
rules.remediation: Return standard HTTP status codes: 201 for Created, 204 for No Content, 400 for Bad Request, 401/403 for Auth, 404 for Not Found, 422 for Unprocessable Entity, and 500 for Internal Errors.

rules.name: Idempotent Mutation Verbs (PUT & DELETE)
rules.description: HTTP PUT and DELETE handlers must guarantee idempotency: executing the same request multiple times must result in the same server state as a single execution.
rules.rationale: Clients frequently retry network requests on transient timeouts; non-idempotent updates cause duplicate mutations.
rules.remediation: Ensure PUT performs total replacement or upsert by resource ID, and DELETE gracefully handles already-deleted resources.
